issues: Covers were 2,034 against 1,754 a year earlier, up 280 (15.96%).
Spend per head was £23.87 against £24.38 a year earlier, down £0.51 (2.09%).
Sales were £49,176.68, beating the £45,500 target by £3,676.68 (8.08%) but down £4,257.41 year on year; the BOH meeting sheet shows £49,465.69 (+8.72%).
Operational labour was 21.1% (£10,398.39) against a 22% target, with labour all in at £12,041.90 (24.49%) and 711.41 hours used.
Drinks mix was 14.20%, sushi 16.52% and sides 13.59%.
Food cost was 22.71%, within target, with food variance at 1.4% and drinks variance at -4.2%.
Labour and sales targets were met with continued steady flow, but weekly spend and compliance remain an issue; the site is not on red light and the quarter percentage is on target.
There were no negative reviews this week (nine 5 star and three 4 star, 4.75 average) against 3.78 with three negatives the week before, after work on service style and staff morale.
Two FOH team members, Aoife and Genoa, are starting supervisor training and cash up training this week, with the additional hours approved within the budget rota.
Friction between FOH and BOH is a pressing issue after a disagreement on Sunday, and the proper procedure for out of stock items has been shared in the group chat.
Morale remains an ongoing issue with some of the team experiencing burnout; the GM will accommodate extra time off where requested, and a night out fund has been approved for team building.
Mapal compliance remained below target last week.
Hygiene compliance continues to dip and remains inconsistent.
FOH and BOH hygiene checks are complete, waste was tracked, sickness and lateness were recorded on Kobas, and budget and Kobas rotas are complete.
A team member is returning to his home country for three months, which will leave labour tight, so labour will be shared between Maki 6 and Maki 8.
There are no further maintenance updates from previous KPIs.
The GM is taking a short holiday from 15/10 to 18/10.
Business outreach by the GM is a continuous task, and fixing morale is the top priority.
XOXO drinks, the lunch deal, app vouchers and student freshers vouchers are the upcoming promotions.

Region-wide (Scotland BOH meeting 06/10): last week's chicken broth usage discrepancy was traced to a takeaway recipe still linked to the old tonkotsu broth in stock counts, which has been corrected, so usage should return to normal next week.

Region-wide (Scotland BOH meeting 06/10): Bidfood is being brought in as a new supplier, starting with Aberdeen and reaching the other sites within one to two months, and new beef samples are being trialled with a view to pre-cooked beef so sites no longer cook it themselves.

Region-wide (Scotland BOH meeting 06/10): frozen ramen promotion stock is delivered from the factory on 07/10, but storage space at the smaller sites is unconfirmed and the memo does not specify quantities per flavour.
